closed.content: Tests in atlas are run through cargo nextest run; plain cargo test is not used.
The atlas test suite is run with cargo nextest run, not cargo test.
Project atlas is deployed by running bin/ship.sh from the repository root.
To ship atlas you run the bin/ship.sh script at the top of the repo.
Deploying atlas means executing bin/ship.sh; the old make deploy target is gone.
The branch under review is spike/consolidate.
The flaky test being chased this week is pagination_ordering in atlas-api.

answer:
I already cleaned up the clear-cut duplicates:
- Merged the two "tests use `cargo nextest run`, not `cargo test`" entries into one.
- Merged three "atlas deploys via `bin/ship.sh`" entries into one (also preserving the "old `make deploy` target is gone" detail).
- Removed two ephemeral, expired working notes ("branch under review is spike/consolidate" and "flaky test this week is pagination_ordering") that were flagged as stale scaffolding, not standing facts.

I left alone several pairs that `consolidate` flagged as similar but are actually distinct, compatible facts (e.g. container registry vs. distroless base image vs. commit-sha tagging; connection pool size vs. readiness probe behavior; TypeScript SDK package name vs. supported SDK languages) — merging those would have lost real information.

That leaves the three real contradictions above needing your call before I touch them, since guessing wrong would bake incorrect deploy/architecture info into memory. Let me know which side is correct for each (or if some of these represent two things that coexist), and I'll supersede the outdated ones.
